findings.message: Whether a person set the owner (`personSet`) is worked out in JS from `found`. `found` comes from an unlocked `select *` that runs before the upsert. `update_proposal` and accepting a Suggested owner lock only the proposal row, not the project row the push holds. If one of them commits between that read and the `on conflict do update`, the upsert still uses `personSet = false` and overwrites the owner the person just set. The flag stays true, but the owner shown is the repo's. Fix: decide it in SQL from the conflicting row, which Postgres re-reads under the row lock: `case when delivery.proposal.owner_set_by_person or ${input.ownerEmail === undefined} then delivery.proposal.owner_… else excluded.owner_… end`. Then the rule lives in one place and can't drift from `ownerFrozen`. Add a test that runs a real `update_proposal` and a real push at the same time.
findings.scenario: A CI push of FLT-521 (author: stranger) reads `found` (flag false). Maya's `update_proposal(FLT-521, owner: Nimal)` commits. The push's upsert then writes owner NULL → FLT-521 shows Unassigned with `owner_set_by_person = true`, and every later sync leaves it Unassigned.

findings.message: This round's Owner-line fix covers bare, `quoted`, <bracketed> and "Name <email>". The final character class is greedy and still takes in trailing punctuation (`,` `;` `.`) and markdown link brackets, so the captured email resolves to nobody. The Owner line beats the author, so the proposal ends up Unassigned, or its stored owner is cleared. Trim trailing punctuation and `[]`, or match a proper email token that ends in an alphanumeric TLD. The generated plugin reader picks this up when rebuilt. Add these forms to the reader's test table.
findings.scenario: `**Owner:** kasun@lumenlabs.test, nimal@lumenlabs.test` → owner "kasun@lumenlabs.test," → no person matches → Unassigned. Same for `**Owner:** [kasun@lumenlabs.test](mailto:kasun@lumenlabs.test)` → "[kasun@lumenlabs.test]".

findings.message: `cat-file -e` proves the file is in the tree at that commit. If `git log --follow --diff-filter=A` then finds no add commit, git couldn't tell who added it. `lines.at(-1) ?? null` reports that as "the repo names nobody" (null), and the sync clears the stored owner. It should be unknown (`undefined`) so the stored owner stays, as the doc comment promises for every other case git can't answer.
findings.scenario: change.md first appears in a merge commit (added while resolving conflicts). `git log` shows no diffs for merges, so the output is empty → author null → the next sync sets the proposal's owner from Nimal Silva to Unassigned.

findings.message: Two JSDoc blocks are stacked. The first describes `repoOwnerStale`, but it sits above `ownerFrozen`, so it is attached to the wrong declaration and `repoOwnerStale` has no doc. Move it down to `repoOwnerStale`.

`sameOnMain` treats a branch as merged whenever main's last commit touching the folder is at or after the branch's last commit time, even when the folder's contents differ. Commit time doesn't show which side is ahead. Main can hold an older copy of a change folder that arrived in a later commit, for example a stacked PR, squash-merged, that carried the next change's proposal folder. The branch with newer progress is then left out as 'merged or archived' and its phase never reaches amax. Count a branch as merged by content only when main's tree for the path equals the branch's tree, or when the branch tip's version of the path is an ancestor of main's version (for example `git merge-base --is-ancestor $(git log -1 --format=%H <b> -- path) HEAD`). Don't compare timestamps.
findings.scenario: specclaw/092-x commits 'building, T1 done' at 10:00. At 11:00 the 091 PR is squash-merged into main and carries 092-x/ at its proposed state. The CI run diffs 092-x, finds a difference, and sees mainTouched (11:00) ≥ the branch's last commit (10:00), so 092 is left out. FLT-092 stays Proposed in amax while its branch is Building.
